$comment: Every (nodeType, accessor, name) the C# extractors read, checked against the
vendored grammar's own src/node-types.json BEFORE any row is produced.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A read that names a node type the grammar does not produce
returns null. It does not throw. The column goes empty, the row count falls
slightly, and nothing anywhere says so. cs-oracle measured the cost of one
instance: childForFieldName('parameters') is a real field on
method_declaration and silently null on class_declaration, which produced 0
primary constructors in a .NET 8 reference app and 173 generic types against
19,567 classes. Both were caught by a human finding the number implausible,
which is luck and does not scale.
It is the structural counterpart of the TypeScript recall probe that reported
99.8-100% across eleven corpora while being incapable of seeing that 31% of
calls were missing. This asserts the instrument can see the thing before any
number exists.
ACCESSORS.
child      satisfied by children.types OR by any field whose types include
the name. node-types.json PARTITIONS contents into fields and
children, but the parse tree exposes a field-bound node as a
named child too, so a by-type child scan finds both. Checking
only children.types is too strict and reports false faults.
field      satisfied only by fields. Stricter, and the accessor that
actually fails silently, so a read declared this way is a
promise that childForFieldName is correct here.
anonymous  an unnamed token, e.g. the `ref` in `ref struct`. node-types.json
does not list anonymous children per parent, so this is checked
against the top-level anonymous node vocabulary only. Weaker,
and stated so rather than pretended otherwise.
mustFail exists so a null result from this gate is known to be a measurement.

recovery   a node the parser produces only on error recovery. node-types.json never lists ERROR or MISSING as a child of anything, so this accessor is RECORDED and NOT verified. Saying so is the point: an unverifiable read that looks verified is worse than one that admits it.
Reconcile with cs-oracle's src/test/csharp-gates/grammar-field-reads.json when
cs-oracle lands on the c-sharp branch: two read-sets is one too many.

reads.name: type_parameter_list
reads.usedBy: cs-type-extractor: ARITY, which is in the PRIMARY KEY. Read as a CHILD and not as the `type_parameters` field, because class/struct/record do not bind that field and the accessor would be silently null on all three.

reads.name: ref
reads.usedBy: cs-type-extractor: isRefLikeStruct. `ref` is NOT a modifier node here.

reads.name: type_parameter_list
reads.usedBy: cs-type-extractor: arity. interface_declaration is the ONE type kind that binds this as a field; the by-type child scan finds it either way, which is why the scan is uniform.

reads.name: struct
reads.usedBy: cs-type-extractor: RECORD vs RECORD_STRUCT. Anonymous, so a modifier scan reports every record as a reference type and inverts the value semantics.

reads.name: parameter_list
reads.usedBy: cs-type-extractor: EXCLUDED from primaryConstructorOf — this is the delegate's signature, not a constructor

reads.name: argument_list
reads.usedBy: cs-heritage-extractor: the FLAT primary-constructor base invocation, as a class writes it

reads.name: primary_constructor_base_type
reads.usedBy: cs-heritage-extractor: the WRAPPED shape, as a record writes it. One construct, two tree shapes — reading only the flat one emitted baseTypeName='Parent(X)' with no row missing anywhere.

reads.name: argument_list
reads.usedBy: cs-heritage-extractor: baseTypeOf skips it to find the type

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-type-parameter-extractor: name (bound as the `name` FIELD, and exposed as a named child)

reads.name: in
reads.usedBy: cs-type-parameter-extractor: variance. Anonymous, so a modifier scan reads every interface as invariant.

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-type-parameter-extractor: the parameter this clause NAMES — constraints are matched by name, not position

reads.name: preproc_arg
reads.usedBy: preproc-context: fileLevelSymbols — the symbol a file-level #define adds (CS-CORPUS-25)

reads.name: preproc_arg
reads.usedBy: preproc-context: fileLevelSymbols — the symbol a file-level #undef removes (CS-CORPUS-25)

reads.name: preproc_elif
reads.usedBy: preproc-context: the chain is NESTED, not flat

reads.name: preproc_else
reads.usedBy: preproc-context: #else is a child of the LAST #elif

reads.name: returns
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: returnTypeOf. A real field here, unlike class_declaration.parameters.

reads.name: explicit_interface_specifier
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: `void IFoo.Bar()` — no accessibility and NOT private

reads.name: type
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: the TARGET type is the only thing distinguishing two conversions on one type

reads.name: implicit
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: conversionKindOf. IMPLICIT runs with NO syntax at the call site.

reads.name: arrow_expression_clause
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: an expression-bodied property has a GETTER and no `get` token. 5,666 sites.

reads.name: type
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor. NOTE: an indexer has NO name field — it is `this[...]`.

reads.name: name
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: get/set/init/add/remove, bound as a FIELD over anonymous tokens

reads.name: modifier
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: `{ get; private set; }` — 581 sites of asymmetric accessibility

reads.name: variable_declaration
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: `event EventHandler A, B;` is N events

reads.name: params
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: `params int[] d` is NOT wrapped in a `parameter` node — it is FLAT siblings of the list, so a scan for `parameter` children drops it entirely. The grammar declares `name` and `type` as multiple FIELDS on the list itself for exactly this case.

reads.name: type
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: unwrapScopedType. `scoped Span<int> f` WRAPS the type; `scoped ref int g` emits a `modifier`. One construct, two shapes — the third on this branch.

reads.name: name
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: a call target a MEMBER walk never reaches, because it is a statement

reads.name: type
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: a REF RETURN hands back an alias, and `ref` lives in the return TYPE, not the modifier list

reads.name: expression
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: containsYield marks an ITERATOR, whose body does not run when it is called

reads.name: array_rank_specifier
reads.usedBy: cs-type-reference-extractor: arrayRank is COMMAS PLUS ONE, not the bracket count

reads.name: tuple_element
reads.usedBy: cs-type-reference-extractor: the elements are CHILDREN because tupleElementCount alone loses their types

reads.name: type
reads.usedBy: cs-type-reference-extractor: reified generics make the argument subtree part of the type's identity

reads.name: generic_name
reads.usedBy: cs-type-reference-extractor: A.B.List<int> puts the ARITY on the LAST segment

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: the interface an explicit implementation is callable through

reads.name: bracketed_parameter_list
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: an indexer's parameters are BRACKETED, and an indexer with no parameters is not an indexer

reads.name: ERROR
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: #else and #endif inside an accessor list arrive as bare ERROR siblings — the grammar produces no preproc_if there. ERROR is a universal recovery node that node-types.json never declares as a child of ANYTHING, so it cannot be checked structurally; declaring it here records the read rather than pretending it is verified.

reads.name: preproc_if_in_attribute_list
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: a #if inside an accessor list is ABSORBED into the first accessor

reads.name: body
reads.usedBy: cs-statement-walker: the node is `foreach_statement`, NOT `for_each_statement`. The wrong name matched nothing, so every expression and every call in every foreach body was invisible — 17% of all call sites in the corpus.

reads.name: condition
reads.usedBy: cs-statement-walker. NOTE: `if` binds its branches as `consequence`/`alternative` FIELDS — there is no `else_clause` node, and declaring one matched nothing.

reads.name: bracketed_argument_list
reads.usedBy: cs-statement-walker: excluded when finding the initializer

reads.name: body
reads.usedBy: cs-expression/member: the BODY FIELD, not a positional guess. A single-parameter lambda writes its parameter as a bare `identifier`, so the positional guess picked the PARAMETER as the body and lost 80% of the corpus's LINQ queries.

reads.name: from_clause
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: LINQ clauses, which the ENGINE desugars

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the `into` CONTINUATION, where an engine must break the desugaring chain

reads.name: name
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the range variable it BINDS

reads.name: join_into_clause
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: a GROUP join is a different operator from a plain join

reads.name: descending
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the grammar gives NO `ordering` node, so a `descending` token applies to the key BEFORE it and one flag on the clause is wrong about the other key

reads.name: tuple_pattern
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: `var (a, b) = t` has no name field

reads.name: using
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: `using var f = …` is the declaration form

reads.name: left
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: the loop variable, or a tuple pattern

reads.name: name
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: `out var n` — a SECOND RETURN CHANNEL

reads.name: name
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: `x is Foo f`; optional, may be a discard

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: deconstruction bindings, flattened in source order

reads.name: discard
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: `var (a, _, b)` binds two, not three

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: `let y = …` exposes no name field

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: the FIRST identifier is the range variable

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: `into g` binds another range variable

reads.name: checked
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: one node type spells checked AND unchecked

reads.name: variable_declaration
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: resourceCount, and the resource local

reads.name: identifier
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: the GOTO TARGET, dropped by TypeScript

reads.name: readonly
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: REF_READONLY — an alias that cannot be written

reads.name: right
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: fork rule 14 mirror — the operand after the #endif; another head when heads are consecutive

reads.name: left
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the taken head’s left operand

reads.name: operator
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the operator at the END of the branch

reads.name: alternative
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor: fork rule 16 — an orphaned else clause’s block is an ELSE block

reads.name: expression
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: fork rule 14 — the receiver a taken chain branch is grafted onto

reads.name: left
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: fork rule 14 operator form — the left operand before the #if

reads.name: operator
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the operator at the START of the branch

reads.name: right
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the taken tail’s right operand

reads.name: parameter_fragment
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: the taken branch’s `T a,` run

reads.name: argument_close_fragment
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: the taken branch that closes the call

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: fork rule 19 — the taken branch holds `expression ;`, taken through takenExpressionOf

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor / cs-block-extractor: fork rule 20 — the initializer through the taken branch

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor / cs-statement-walker: fork rule 21 — a #if among switch sections, resolved by the walks’ preproc handling

reads.name: switch_section
reads.usedBy: cs-block-extractor / cs-statement-walker: the taken branch’s sections

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: cs-statement-walker: fork rule 21 label form — the label under a #if

reads.name: switch_label
reads.usedBy: cs-statement-walker: the taken branch’s stacked label, CASE_LABEL context

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: cs-heritage-extractor: fork rule 22 — a continuation under a #if

reads.name: base_continuation
reads.usedBy: cs-heritage-extractor: the taken branch’s `, T` run

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: cs-expression-extractor: fork rule 27 — arms under a #if

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: cs-type-parameter-extractor: fork rule 28 — a where clause under a #if (also on class/struct/interface/record/delegate/local function declarations)

reads.name: base_fragment
reads.usedBy: cs-heritage-extractor: fork rule 29 — the taken branch’s `T,` run

reads.name: modifier
reads.usedBy: preproc-context: modifiersOf — fork rule 31, the taken branch’s modifiers

reads.name: preproc_if
reads.usedBy: preproc-context: modifiersOf — a #if holding modifiers (also on every other declaration that repeats them)

reads.name: type
reads.usedBy: cs-member-extractor: throughTakenBranch — a return type under a #if

reads.name: constraint_continuation
reads.usedBy: cs-type-parameter-extractor: fork rule 35 — the taken branch’s `, constraint` run

mustFail.name: type_parameters
mustFail.why: THE BUG AS WRITTEN. interface_declaration binds this field and class_declaration does not, so the identical call site is right for interfaces and silently null for classes, structs and records. Arity is in cs_type's PRIMARY KEY, so it would fork the identity of every generic class.

mustFail.name: parameters
mustFail.why: the same shape on primary constructors. A real field on method_declaration, absent here, and the failure is a null.

mustFail.name: no_such_node_type
mustFail.why: a plain misspelling must be caught, or the gate is only testing the two cases someone already knew about.

mustFail.name: name
mustFail.why: an indexer has NO name — it is `this[...]`. Reading one returns null and the property row would be named the empty string, which every other indexer on the type would also be.

mustFail.name: not_a_recovery_node
mustFail.why: the recovery accessor is the weakest of the three and must still be able to say no, or it becomes a way to smuggle any read past the gate.

mustFail.name: for_each_statement
mustFail.why: THE BUG AS WRITTEN. The statement walker's table said `for_each_statement`; the grammar's node is `foreach_statement`. It matched nothing, and every expression and call inside every foreach body was invisible — 17% of the corpus's call sites, with no count able to see it because the enclosing method's other statements were all present.
